name: MK-677

lead: MK-677 (ibutamoren) is an orally active, non-peptide drug that mimics ghrelin and raises growth hormone and IGF-1. It was developed by Merck but never approved, and is sold as a research chemical.
Trials in older adults and obese men showed increased fat-free mass but no clear functional improvement, and no cosmetic benefit has been demonstrated; the wiki's rating is unproven.

paras: It activates the ghrelin receptor (GHS-R1a) in the pituitary and hypothalamus, producing pulsatile growth hormone release and downstream IGF-1 elevation, plus increased appetite.

Not approved for any use and prohibited in sport. Reported effects include increased appetite, fluid retention, lethargy and reduced insulin sensitivity; a heart failure signal appeared in one trial. Long-term effects of sustained IGF-1 elevation are unknown, and products may be mislabelled.
